blurb:
If you haven't caught Malcolm Todd live yet, the Roxy on September 12 is a good place to start.

Todd has built a following the old-fashioned way, through relentless touring and a sound that sits somewhere between indie folk and Americana in a way that actually holds up at volume in a real venue. The Coca-Cola Roxy is one of the better mid-size rooms in Atlanta, close enough to feel intimate, big enough to have real production behind it. Show runs 8:00 to 11:30 PM, so there's plenty of time to grab dinner in the Battery beforehand.

Saturday night, good room, artist on the rise. That's a solid combo.
scoring_notes: Fits the younger adult segment of the Perimeter Post audience well. Malcolm Todd is an emerging artist so there's some discovery appeal, though he's not a household name that drives urgency for the broader audience. Saturday night timing and Battery location are strong practical factors.

event_name: What's With Atlanta? Author Talk with Paige Watts
blurb:
Why is every street in Atlanta named Peachtree? Why does the city completely shut down when there's a quarter inch of snow? These are real questions, and Paige Watts has real answers.

The Georgia Room at Switzer Library is hosting Watts for an author talk on Monday the 14th from 6:00 to 7:00 PM. She's written about Atlanta's quirks, history, and identity in a way that's actually fun to read, not a dry civic history lesson. If you've lived here for any amount of time, you've wondered about half the things she covers. This is the chance to hear the explanations in person and probably laugh at a few of them.

Free, local, and genuinely interesting. Hard to argue with that combination.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the educated, community-connected segment of this audience. Free admission removes any barrier. The Atlanta-centric subject matter plays well to people who are invested in the region. Weeknight timing and library setting skew slightly older but work well for the mixed adult crowd.

event_name: Kintsugi Experience with Eva Crawford at dk Gallery
blurb:
Kintsugi is the Japanese art of repairing broken things with gold, treating the cracks as part of the history rather than something to hide. It's a great philosophy and, it turns out, a genuinely satisfying thing to do with your hands for a couple of hours.

Artist Eva Crawford leads this hands-on experience at dk Gallery in Marietta on Thursday the 24th from 2:00 to 4:30 PM. You'll learn the technique, work through the process yourself, and walk away with something you actually made. It's a ticketed event with limited spots, which means it's intimate by design. Not a class where you watch someone demonstrate from across the room.

For the empty nesters and anyone who's been looking for something a little more creative to fill a weekday afternoon, this is a good one.
scoring_notes: Hands-on art experience with a cultural concept behind it fits the educated adult segment well. Weekday afternoon timing skews toward empty nesters rather than young professionals. Concept and execution are genuinely unique for the area, which pushes the uniqueness score up.

blurb:
Six wines, heavy appetizers, and someone who actually knows what they're talking about walking you through all of it. That's the whole evening.

Deep Roots Wine Market on Marietta Square is hosting a guided tasting featuring Valdemar Estates on September 15, running from 6:30 to 8:30 PM. You'll taste six featured wines alongside food from Gianni and Mac's, with the kind of in-depth conversation about what you're drinking that turns a Tuesday night into something worth putting on the calendar. At $40 a ticket (or $30 for wine club members), it's a STEAL for what you're getting.

Small, intimate, and exactly the kind of thing that sells out before people realize they missed it. Grab tickets through Deep Roots directly.
scoring_notes: Wine tasting events with food pairings are a strong fit for the educated, higher-income adult segment of this audience. $40 price point is very accessible for a $105K median income household. Weeknight timing and Marietta Square location (slightly outside core Perimeter) are minor considerations.

event_name: Thee Sacred Souls at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Thee Sacred Souls play soul music the way soul music is supposed to sound, warm, tight, and built for a room full of people who actually want to listen.

The San Diego trio has become one of the most talked-about acts in the genre over the last few years, drawing comparisons to classic 60s and 70s soul while putting out music that sounds completely current. They hit the Coca-Cola Roxy on Tuesday the 15th, which is admittedly a weeknight, but some shows are worth rearranging the schedule for. This is one of those.

If you've been sleeping on them, consider this your wake-up call.
scoring_notes: Thee Sacred Souls has strong credibility and a growing following among the 30-45 demographic. The soul/R&B genre skews toward the educated adult segment of this audience well. Weeknight timing is a moderate drag on attendance appeal but the artist's uniqueness compensates.

venue: ASW Distillery at the Battery, Atlanta
blurb:
You've probably had a cocktail at ASW. You've probably never made one there. That changes September 20.

ASW's monthly cocktail class puts you at your own fully stocked bar station with tools, ingredients, and one of their lead mixologists walking you through how to actually build a drink from scratch. You'll make three cocktails over the 90-minute class, covering whiskey, vodka, and gin, learning the balance and technique that separates a real cocktail from a pour-and-hope situation. It's hands-on the whole way through, not a demo you watch from a stool.

Good date night, good group activity, and you'll leave actually knowing what you're doing the next time someone asks you to make a round. Space fills up, so grab your spot.
scoring_notes: Extremely strong fit for the young professional and adult segments of this audience. Interactive, social, adult-oriented, and priced well within reach for a $105K median income household. The Battery location makes it easy and familiar. Recurring monthly format is the only knock on uniqueness.

event_name: Guns N' Roses at Truist Park
blurb:
There are concerts, and then there are Guns N' Roses concerts. This is the second kind.

The 2026 World Tour rolls into Truist Park on September 19 for one night only. Axl, Slash, and the rest of the band are still doing it at a level most acts half their age can't touch, and an outdoor stadium show at Truist is genuinely one of the best setups in Atlanta for a big rock night. Good sightlines, the Battery right there if you want to grab dinner first, and the kind of crowd energy that only happens when everyone in the building grew up on the same songs.

If you were ever a Welcome to the Jungle kid, this is your night. Get tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 means this audience grew up on GNR in the 90s. Stadium rock is a strong fit for the mixed adult crowd. One-night-only at a major outdoor venue makes it genuinely can't-miss. Income supports variable ticket pricing.

event_name: Don't Be Cruel: The Elvis Experience
blurb: Sunday afternoon at the Jennie T. Anderson Theatre and Elvis is in the house. Don't Be Cruel: The Elvis Experience brings the King's catalog to life on September 20th in Marietta, and for the right crowd, this is a really fun two hours. Cobb Parks puts on quality productions at this venue, and a well-executed Elvis tribute hits different in a theater setting than you'd expect. It's a Sunday at 3pm, which makes it easy to fold into the rest of the weekend without any complicated logistics. Good music, local venue, low effort to get there. If your household has an Elvis fan, this is an easy gift of an afternoon.
scoring_notes: Elvis tribute appeal skews toward the older end of East Cobb's demographic, which fits the empty nester segment well. Jennie T. Anderson is a familiar, trusted local venue. Sunday afternoon timing is very accessible. Lower uniqueness score since it's a tribute act rather than a rare or one-of-a-kind event.

blurb: StillFire Smyrna is throwing their first-ever Oktoberfest this weekend, and they're doing it properly. Two days of German-inspired craft beer, live music, traditional games, and a best-dressed contest for anyone willing to show up in lederhosen or a dirndl. Saturday runs from 1pm to 7pm with two back-to-back live acts. Sunday brings the Class Act German Band from 3 to 6pm. It's a two-day run, which means if Saturday doesn't work, you've got a second shot. StillFire has built a solid following in the area, and their inaugural Oktoberfest is the kind of thing that gets more crowded every year once people figure out it exists. Show up for the first one. Prost.
scoring_notes: Inaugural event gives it genuine first-year uniqueness. Smyrna is close enough to East Cobb to be relevant. Strong adult/empty nester appeal. Free admission with drinks purchased separately is low-barrier. Not quite as premium as other candidates but a fun, social pick for the weekend.

blurb: This is not your typical weekend activity, and that's exactly the point. The Bladesmithing 101 two-day workshop at Art Center West in Roswell puts you at a forge with a hammer in your hand, learning how to shape, heat, and finish a three-piece knife set from scratch. The curriculum covers everything from material selection and forging technique to heat treating and finishing. You walk out with something you made yourself, using tools most people have never touched. If you or someone in your house has been curious about metalworking, blacksmithing, or just doing something with your hands that's genuinely different, this one's worth looking into. Spots are limited by the nature of the class. Check availability and book before it fills.
scoring_notes: Extremely high uniqueness, this is a hands-on craft experience you can't replicate with a Google search. Roswell location is ideal for East Cobb readers. Strong appeal to the educated, curious demographic and to households with older teens who might attend with a parent. Weekend-long commitment filters for serious interest.

blurb: Sixty years is not a small number. The Roswell Arts Festival has been running since the 1960s, which makes this year's edition something worth actually marking on the calendar rather than just scrolling past. It runs from 11am to 6pm on Saturday at Roswell City Hall, with artists and vendors spread across one of the better historic backdrops in the Atlanta metro. This is the kind of afternoon that's easy to make a day out of, especially if you finish it with dinner somewhere nearby in Canton Street. Bring the family, bring a friend, or go alone with nowhere to be. It's free, it's close, and after 60 years, it clearly does something right.
scoring_notes: 60th anniversary gives a recurring festival meaningful uniqueness this year. Roswell is right next door to East Cobb. Free admission removes any barrier. Appeals to the arts-educated demographic and families with older kids. Saturday daytime timing is highly accessible.

event_name: Folsom Prison Live! The Johnny Cash Experience
blurb: Sunday afternoon in Marietta, and Johnny Cash is in the building. Folsom Prison Live! brings the Man in Black's legendary concert experience to the Jennie T. Anderson Theatre on September 13th, and for anyone who grew up on that music, this is a genuinely fun afternoon out. The Folsom Prison album is one of the most iconic live recordings in American music history, and a tribute done well captures something real about it. This is a Cobb Parks production, which means it's local, it's accessible, and it's the kind of thing you can bring your parents to, or go with a group, without any complicated logistics. Easy Sunday. Good music. Go.
scoring_notes: Johnny Cash appeals strongly to East Cobb's 42-median-age crowd and older empty nesters. Jennie T. Anderson is a well-known local venue. Sunday afternoon timing is approachable. Cobb Parks programming tends to be well-priced. Not as rare as a one-night headliner but locally produced and easy to attend.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb: Atlanta Ballet is opening its new season right here at the Cobb Energy Centre on September 18th, and this is a program worth showing up for. Three distinct works on one stage: a world influenced by the art and music of Fanny Mendelssohn-Hensel and Sonia Delaunay, a brand new piece set to Tchaikovsky, and Balanchine's Stars and Stripes, which is exactly the kind of big, joyful finale you leave humming. It's also a 250th anniversary celebration of American history woven into the closer, so the whole program has a sense of occasion to it. If you've been meaning to get to the ballet but haven't made a plan, here's your plan. Tickets are available now.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the educated, higher-income East Cobb demographic. Cobb Energy Centre is local. Season opener with three distinct programs gives it more substance than a typical single-work performance. Adult and empty nester skew makes this a solid pick for that segment of the audience.

event_name: Guns N' Roses at Truist Park
blurb: If you grew up with a cassette copy of Appetite for Destruction rattling around in your car, this one's been a long time coming. Guns N' Roses is playing Truist Park on Saturday night, and that's not a normal Saturday night. This is the real lineup, the kind of show that doesn't come around every year, and it's happening right in your backyard at one of the best outdoor venues in the country. Expect the classics: Welcome to the Jungle, Paradise City, November Rain. All of it, loud, in the open air. Get your tickets now. These are not sitting around.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's median age is 42, which puts the core audience squarely in peak Guns N' Roses nostalgia territory. At $118K household income, ticket prices are not a barrier. Truist Park is geographically close. One-night show with massive name recognition makes this the highest uniqueness score of the batch.

blurb: This is the kind of dinner you don't stumble across very often. The William Root House is opening after hours on Saturday evening for a candlelit, multi-course dinner on the grounds of one of Marietta's oldest antebellum homes. Private after-hours museum access, chef-prepared dishes from 1885 Grill, and an intimate crowd, because space is genuinely limited. The menu runs from sweet potato tartlets and arugula salad through grilled chicken with pumpkin romesco, all the way to maple praline bread pudding. You can bring your own wine or cocktails. At $90 per person for a 2-person table, it's an easy yes for a date night that actually feels different. The 2-person tables are already sold out, but 4-person tables are still available. Grab three people you actually want to sit across from and make a reservation before those go too.
scoring_notes: Perfectly tuned for East Cobb's established family and empty nester demographic. After-hours access to a historic Marietta landmark is genuinely rare. Price point is completely accessible at $118K median income. Limited seating makes it a real can't-miss. Best fit for the date-night or couples segment of the audience.

event_name: Sunset Sips at the Chattahoochee Nature Center
time: Doors open 6:00 PM, Music at 7:00 PM
blurb:
This is a genuinely good evening out for people who don't want to drive far or fight a crowd. Sunset Sips at the Chattahoochee Nature Center is exactly what it sounds like: a Thursday night on the Great Lawn, cash bar in hand, live music starting at 7, and the kind of late-summer sunset that makes you remember why you chose to live out here.

Before the music kicks in, you've got extended hours to walk the Wildlife Walk, the River Boardwalk, and the shaded trails. It's a rare chance to see the Nature Center in a completely different light, literally. CNC members get in free and can reserve tickets online. Not a member yet? Walk-up admission is available as capacity allows, though advance tickets are the smarter move. Thursday nights don't have to feel like a Tuesday.
scoring_notes: The Chattahoochee Nature Center is almost literally in East Cobb's backyard. Evening hours, a cash bar, and live music skew adult and fit the empty nester and established-family crowd perfectly. The nature walk element adds something you can't replicate at a bar or restaurant. Strong local identity match.
